**Rebuttal (Debater B)**

Debater A and I agree on the value, since n(2^{n-1} − 1) + 1 and (2^{n-1}·n − n) + 1 are the same number. The dispute is whether the argument justifies it, and B's argument is the one you can check.

A's lower bound asserts "A_t ≡ 1 (mod 2^{n-1})" and "p_t + q_t + 2r_t = 2^n − 1" without defining A_t, q_t, or r_t, so the failure of the uniform configuration at every target is never shown. B's version is explicit. The invariant w = Σ 2^u p_u (mod 2^n − 1) fixes the required pile residues r_j, and the potential Φ_j gives the criterion "unstackable iff Φ_j < r_j for all j." For the uniform configuration, Φ_j = 2^n − 1 − (2^n − 1)/2^{n-1} < 2^n − 1 = r_j, which you can verify directly.

A's upper bound, N + R ≤ n·2^{n-1}, is stated with no derivation. B derives the bound in both cases. If w ≡ 0, summing the scaled potentials Φ̃_j ≡ 0 (mod 2^n − 1) gives t ≤ n(2^{n-1} − 1). If w ≢ 0, B gets t < (n−1)2^{n-1}, which is no larger.

A's only independent check is n = 2. B also reports n = 3, where the largest unstackable total is 9, giving stack = 10.
